The **67th Annual Grammy Awards** honored the best recordings, compositions, and artists from September 16, 2023, to August 30, 2024, as chosen by the members of [the Recording Academy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Recording_Academy "The Recording Academy"), on February 2, 2025.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Annual_Grammy_Awards#cite_note-2) In its 22nd year at [Crypto.com Arena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crypto.com_Arena "Crypto.com Arena") in [Los Angeles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles "Los Angeles"), the main ceremony was broadcast on [CBS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CBS "CBS") and available to stream on [Paramount+](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paramount+ "Paramount+"). It was preceded by the premiere ceremony at the [Peacock Theater](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peacock_Theater "Peacock Theater"), starting at 12:30 p.m. PT. Nominations were announced through a [YouTube](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YouTube "YouTube") livestream on November 8, 2024.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Annual_Grammy_Awards#cite_note-3) The South African comedian [Trevor Noah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Noah "Trevor Noah") hosted the ceremony for the fifth consecutive time.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Annual_Grammy_Awards#cite_note-4)
[Kendrick Lamar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kendrick_Lamar "Kendrick Lamar")'s "[Not Like Us](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us "Not Like Us")" swept all five of its nominations, which included [Record of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Record_of_the_Year "Grammy Award for Record of the Year") and [Song of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Song_of_the_Year "Grammy Award for Song of the Year"), tying with "[Up, Up and Away](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Up,_Up_and_Away_\(song\) "Up, Up and Away \(song\)")" to become the joint-most decorated song in Grammy Awards history. He became the second rap artist to win both awards, after [Childish Gambino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Childish_Gambino "Childish Gambino") in [2019](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/61st_Annual_Grammy_Awards "61st Annual Grammy Awards").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Annual_Grammy_Awards#cite_note-5) [Beyoncé](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beyonc%C3%A9 "Beyoncé") received the most nominations at the ceremony with eleven and won three awards, including [Album of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Album_of_the_Year "Grammy Award for Album of the Year") and [Best Country Album](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Best_Country_Album "Grammy Award for Best Country Album") for _[Cowboy Carter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter "Cowboy Carter")_. She became the first Black artist to win Best Country Album and the first Black woman to win Album of the Year since [Lauryn Hill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lauryn_Hill "Lauryn Hill") in [1999](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/41st_Annual_Grammy_Awards "41st Annual Grammy Awards").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Annual_Grammy_Awards#cite_note-6) [Chappell Roan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chappell_Roan "Chappell Roan") took home [Best New Artist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Best_New_Artist "Grammy Award for Best New Artist"), and [Sierra Ferrell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sierra_Ferrell "Sierra Ferrell") swept the American roots categories, winning all four of her nominations.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Annual_Grammy_Awards#cite_note-7) Best New Artist nominee [Doechii](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doechii "Doechii") won [Best Rap Album](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Rap_Album "Best Rap Album") for _[Alligator Bites Never Heal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alligator_Bites_Never_Heal "Alligator Bites Never Heal"),_ becoming the third woman to win the award after Hill (with the [Fugees](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fugees "Fugees")) in [1997](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/39th_Annual_Grammy_Awards "39th Annual Grammy Awards") and [Cardi B](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardi_B "Cardi B") in [2019](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/61st_Annual_Grammy_Awards "61st Annual Grammy Awards"). Other three-time winners included [Charli XCX](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charli_XCX "Charli XCX") and [St. Vincent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Vincent_\(musician\) "St. Vincent \(musician\)"). Other artists that led nominations included Charli XCX and [Post Malone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone "Post Malone") with eight each, and Kendrick Lamar and [Billie Eilish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billie_Eilish "Billie Eilish") with seven each.
## Background
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=67th_Annual_Grammy_Awards&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Background")]
For the 2025 ceremony, the Recording Academy announced several changes [for different categories](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Grammy_Award_categories "List of Grammy Award categories") and updates on eligibility rules.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Annual_Grammy_Awards#cite_note-8) No new categories were introduced for the first time in four years.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Annual_Grammy_Awards#cite_note-9) In an urgent letter to the 12,000 voting members of the Recording Academy, [chief executive officer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chief_executive_officer "Chief executive officer") (CEO) [Harvey Mason Jr.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harvey_Mason_Jr. "Harvey Mason Jr.") urged them to cast their votes with "purpose, [intention](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intention "Intention"), and [integrity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Integrity "Integrity")" and without "bias, grudge-holding, or careless voting".[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Annual_Grammy_Awards#cite_note-10)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Annual_Grammy_Awards#cite_note-11)
Discussions were held to either postpone the ceremony and all of its ancillary events or pivot the broadcast to a [fundraiser](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fundraising "Fundraising") due to the [series of wildfires affecting Southern California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/January_2025_Southern_California_wildfires "January 2025 Southern California wildfires").[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Annual_Grammy_Awards#cite_note-12)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Annual_Grammy_Awards#cite_note-13) In a joint statement, Mason Jr. and Tammy Hurt, the chair of the Recording Academy's board of trustees, confirmed that the ceremony would proceed as planned "in close coordination with local authorities to ensure public safety and responsible use of area resources."[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Annual_Grammy_Awards#cite_note-14) This edition, however, carried a "renewed sense of purpose: raising additional funds to support wildfire relief efforts and honoring the bravery and dedication of [first responders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_responder "First responder") who risk their lives to protect ours."[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Annual_Grammy_Awards#cite_note-15)
During the broadcast, some commercial airtime was donated to help small businesses affected by the wildfires. Host Trevor Noah announced this initiative and special guests appeared in the commercials. Featured businesses included Orla Floral Studio of [Altadena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Altadena,_California "Altadena, California") with an appearance by [Doja Cat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doja_Cat "Doja Cat"), Two Dragons Martial Arts of Altadena with an appearance by [Charlie Puth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlie_Puth "Charlie Puth"), Rhythms Of The Village of Altadena with an appearance by [Anderson .Paak](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anderson_.Paak "Anderson .Paak"), Paliskates Skate Shop in [Pacific Palisades](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pacific_Palisades,_Los_Angeles "Pacific Palisades, Los Angeles") with an appearance by [Avril Lavigne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Avril_Lavigne "Avril Lavigne"), and the L.A. Lost Stuffy Project with an appearance by the [Jonas Brothers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jonas_Brothers "Jonas Brothers").[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Annual_Grammy_Awards#cite_note-16)
Additionally, high school choir students from [Pasadena Waldorf School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pasadena_Waldorf_School "Pasadena Waldorf School") in Altadena and [Palisades Charter High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palisades_Charter_High_School "Palisades Charter High School") in the Pacific Palisades, both of which were damaged in the wildfires, sang backup vocals during the [Stevie Wonder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stevie_Wonder "Stevie Wonder") and [Herbie Hancock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Herbie_Hancock "Herbie Hancock") performance of "[We Are the World](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/We_Are_the_World "We Are the World")."[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Annual_Grammy_Awards#cite_note-17)
### Category changes
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=67th_Annual_Grammy_Awards&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Category changes")]
  * [Best Remixed Recording, Non-Classical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Best_Remixed_Recording,_Non-Classical "Grammy Award for Best Remixed Recording, Non-Classical") was moved from the Production, Engineering, Composition & Arrangement Field to the Pop & Dance/Electronic Field.
  * Best Pop Dance Recording was renamed to [Best Dance Pop Recording](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Best_Dance_Pop_Recording "Grammy Award for Best Dance Pop Recording").
  * Best Dance/Electronic Music Album was renamed to [Best Dance/Electronic Album](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Best_Dance/Electronic_Album "Grammy Award for Best Dance/Electronic Album"). Its category criteria was amended to establish that albums must consist of at least 50% Dance/Electronic recordings to qualify.
  * [Conjunto music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conjunto "Conjunto") will now be recognized under [Best Regional Roots Music Album](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Best_Regional_Roots_Music_Album "Grammy Award for Best Regional Roots Music Album"), instead of [Best Música Mexicana Album (Including Tejano)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Best_M%C3%BAsica_Mexicana_Album_\(including_Tejano\) "Grammy Award for Best Música Mexicana Album \(including Tejano\)").
  * [Best Score Soundtrack for Video Games and Other Interactive Media](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Best_Score_Soundtrack_for_Video_Games_and_Other_Interactive_Media "Grammy Award for Best Score Soundtrack for Video Games and Other Interactive Media") was amended to establish a qualification that more than 50% of the music on an otherwise eligible recording must be derived from new episodes or new programming released during the Grammy eligibility year for which it entered.
  * Best Song for Social Change, a Special Merit Award, was renamed to the [Harry Belafonte](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harry_Belafonte "Harry Belafonte") Best Song for Social Change Award. It will now be recognized as a CEO's Merit Award, with the finalists and recipients selected annually by a committee composed of a community of peers dedicated to "artistic expression, the craft of songwriting, and the power of songs to affect [social change](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Social_change "Social change")."[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Annual_Grammy_Awards#cite_note-Belafonte-18)


### Criteria amendments
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=67th_Annual_Grammy_Awards&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Criteria amendments")]
  * All eligibly-certified featured artists with less than 50% of playing time will be awarded a Winners' Certificate for all genre album categories. This rule does not apply to [Best Musical Theater Album](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Best_Musical_Theater_Album "Grammy Award for Best Musical Theater Album") or the General Field and Craft categories.
  * The annual fee media companies must pay to enter a recording in the online entry process was increased to $180.
  * Criteria for [Best Traditional R&B Performance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Best_Traditional_R&B_Performance "Grammy Award for Best Traditional R&B Performance") was amended to "more accurately represent recordings that embody the classical elements of [R&B](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhythm_and_blues "Rhythm and blues")/[soul music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soul_music "Soul music"), distinguishing them from [contemporary interpretations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Contemporary_R&B "Contemporary R&B") of the genre."
  * Criteria for [Best Traditional Pop Vocal Album](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Best_Traditional_Pop_Vocal_Album "Grammy Award for Best Traditional Pop Vocal Album") was amended to expand the category by "broadening its scope and welcoming more entries from the [musical theater](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Musical_theatre "Musical theatre") community." Its album eligibility criteria was also updated, requiring that albums must contain more than 75% of newly recorded (previously unreleased) performances.
  * Criteria for [Best Children's Music Album](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Best_Children's_Music_Album "Grammy Award for Best Children's Music Album") was amended with a requirement for lyrics and English-language translations to be included in entry submissions. An intended audience range was also defined as "[infant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Infant "Infant") to [12 years old](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Preadolescence "Preadolescence")".
  * Submission guidelines for [Songwriter of the Year, Non-Classical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Songwriter_of_the_Year,_Non-Classical "Grammy Award for Songwriter of the Year, Non-Classical") were amended with the hopes of allowing a "wider representation of the songwriter community", with the minimum submission threshold in which a songwriter is credited as a songwriter or co-writer (not a primary or featured artist or producer) being reduced from five to four songs. The additional number of songs a songwriter may enter in which they are also credited as a primary or featured artist, or any other supporting role was also increased from four to five.

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=67th_Annual_Grammy_Awards&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Winners and nominees")]
First round voting took place from October 4 to October 15, 2024. The nominees were announced by [Brandy Clark](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brandy_Clark "Brandy Clark"), [Kirk Franklin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kirk_Franklin "Kirk Franklin"), [David Frost](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Frost_\(producer\) "David Frost \(producer\)"), [Robert Gordon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Gordon_\(singer\) "Robert Gordon \(singer\)"), [Kylie Minogue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kylie_Minogue "Kylie Minogue"), [Victoria Monét](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victoria_Mon%C3%A9t "Victoria Monét"), [Gaby Moreno](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaby_Moreno "Gaby Moreno"), Deanie Parker, [Mark Ronson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Ronson "Mark Ronson"), [Ben Platt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Platt "Ben Platt"), and [Hayley Williams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hayley_Williams "Hayley Williams") on November 8 in a livestream on the official Grammy [YouTube](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YouTube "YouTube") channel.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Annual_Grammy_Awards#cite_note-29)[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Annual_Grammy_Awards#cite_note-grammy1-30) Final round voting then took place from December 12, 2024, to January 3, 2025, ahead of when the winners were revealed during the Grammy Premiere Ceremony and telecast on February 2.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Annual_Grammy_Awards#cite_note-31)[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Annual_Grammy_Awards#cite_note-32)
[Beyoncé](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beyonc%C3%A9 "Beyoncé") received the most nominations with eleven, which set a new one-year record for nominations by a female artist. She previously shared the record with [Lauryn Hill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lauryn_Hill "Lauryn Hill"), who earned 10 nominations at the [1999](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/41st_Annual_Grammy_Awards "41st Annual Grammy Awards") ceremony, and matched it herself in [2010](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/52nd_Annual_Grammy_Awards "52nd Annual Grammy Awards").[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Annual_Grammy_Awards#cite_note-33)[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Annual_Grammy_Awards#cite_note-34) With a career total of 99 nominations, Beyoncé became the [most nominated artist in Grammy history](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_milestones#Most_Grammy_nominations "Grammy Award milestones"), breaking a tie with her husband [Jay-Z](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jay-Z "Jay-Z").[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Annual_Grammy_Awards#cite_note-35) [Taylor Swift](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift "Taylor Swift") is the first woman to earn seven career nominations for [Album of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Album_of_the_Year "Grammy Award for Album of the Year") with _[The Tortured Poets Department](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Tortured_Poets_Department "The Tortured Poets Department")_.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Annual_Grammy_Awards#cite_note-36) "[Now and Then](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Now_and_Then_\(Beatles_song\) "Now and Then \(Beatles song\)")" by [the Beatles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Beatles "The Beatles") is the first song produced with the help of [artificial intelligence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artificial_intelligence "Artificial intelligence") to be nominated for a Grammy.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Annual_Grammy_Awards#cite_note-37) [Anitta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anitta_\(singer\) "Anitta \(singer\)")'s _[Funk Generation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Funk_Generation "Funk Generation")_ is the first [funk carioca](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Funk_carioca "Funk carioca") album to be nominated for a Grammy.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Annual_Grammy_Awards#cite_note-38) [Sabrina Carpenter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sabrina_Carpenter "Sabrina Carpenter") and [Chappell Roan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chappell_Roan "Chappell Roan") became the fourteenth and fifteenth artists in history [who have earned Grammy nominations in all four main General Field categories in one night](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_milestones#Artists_who_had_been_nominated_for_all_four_General_Field_awards_in_one_night "Grammy Award milestones"). [Charli XCX](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charli_XCX "Charli XCX") and [Post Malone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone "Post Malone") were added to the nominees for [Best Recording Package](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Best_Recording_Package "Grammy Award for Best Recording Package") for their respective albums on December 20.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Annual_Grammy_Awards#cite_note-39) At [100 years of age](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Centenarian "Centenarian"), former U.S. president [Jimmy Carter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Carter "Jimmy Carter") became the oldest nominee ever;[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Annual_Grammy_Awards#cite_note-40) he won [Best Audio Book, Narration & Storytelling Recording](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Best_Audio_Book,_Narration_&_Storytelling_Recording "Grammy Award for Best Audio Book, Narration & Storytelling Recording") for the fourth time, more than any other recipient to date,[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Annual_Grammy_Awards#cite_note-41) which would have made him the [oldest winner ever](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_milestones#Oldest_winners "Grammy Award milestones") if not for [his death](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Death_and_state_funeral_of_Jimmy_Carter "Death and state funeral of Jimmy Carter") in December 2024.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Annual_Grammy_Awards#cite_note-42)
Winners appear first and highlighted in **bold**.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Annual_Grammy_Awards#cite_note-43)
